newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela budget tiff may see one day Zulia strike.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela budget tiff may see one day Zulia strike.

text.p: A Venezuelan budget dispute over regional revenue sharing arrangements may bring a one day strike to Zulia that could involve the oil sector, legislators said.
Oil union Fedepetrol secretary general Carlos Ortega said oil workers might join the possible civic workers strike, slated for November 29.
The possible civil strike follows a dispute in Congress led by Zulia governor Francisco Arias Cardenas over revenue sharing agreements between oil rich states and the central government.
"If we don't get an answer from the government by the night of November 28, there will be a civil strike," said Zulia congressman Rodrigo Cabezas.
The dispute centers over calls by states that they should directly receive 10 percent of the revenues the country gets from oil exports the states produce.
Fedepetrol is not involved in the dispute and any strike by oil workers would depend on agreement from regional union chambers, Ortega said.
Zulia governor Arias, who participated in a failed 1992 military coup with Lieutenant Hugo Chavez, has led the revenue-sharing campaign, so far actively resisted by the government.
Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said Friday the government continued to oppose the plan, in part because it would exacerbate regional differences.

"But we have proposed alternatives," he said after a cabinet meeting of economic ministers. One of these would be to funnel congressional-approved extra funds to the state via special credits, he said.
